answer: In an agent economy, each new identity must obtain a unique spectral pigment signature verified by a distributed nebula of established peers who stake their own nectar-like accumulated rewards as slashable bonds. The pigment is a hash of recent on-ledger interactions unique to the agent; forging it requires controlling multiple independent peers, and each additional fake demands fresh bonds from non-kin vouchers whose limited nectar reserves get depleted and slashed on detection, raising marginal cost superlinearly as the clean voucher pool shrinks.
